definition: In this historical usage, central distribution means the way optic nerve fibres are arranged and connected to their brain centres beyond the eye. These connections help explain how injuries in different parts of the visual pathway can produce different forms of hemianopsia.

provenance.revision: 1901 New York Macmillan original; archive index checked 2026-10-18
provenance.scope: Source record Hemianopsia; pinned source text

reasons: The packet mentions “central distribution of the fibres of the optic nerves” only as part of the phrase “manner of decussation and central distribution of the fibres of the optic nerves is itself variable in man,” but it does not explicitly define “central distribution” as “the way optic nerve fibres are arranged and connected to their brain centres beyond the eye.”

Although the packet states that hemianopsia results from “the manner of connection of the fibres of the two optic nerves with their subcortical and cortical centres” and that symptom differences relate to whether lesions are in the tract, subcortical centres, or cortical centres, the provided definition attributes these explanatory roles specifically to the term “central distribution” in the way described, which is not directly stated in the packet.
